# character-portrait

Purpose: Plan a character-portrait scene (subject, pose, expression, wardrobe, framing, lighting, background) before any modeling or render attempt.

Translate a single-subject character-portrait intent (subject identity, pose, expression, wardrobe, framing, lighting, background) into a structured scene plan with an explicit assumptions register. Distinct from `product-hero-scene-planner` (manufactured products), `environment-shot` (places), and `interior-scene` (rooms). Multi-character ensembles are out of scope. Hands off framing deep-dives to `camera-composition`, lookdev deep-dives to `lighting-material-plan`, assets to `asset-discovery`, and validation to `composition-quality-checker`, `lighting-quality-checker`, and `scene-readiness`.

Metadata: Contract `v1.0.0` | Category `scene-planners` | Role `character-portrait-and-turntable-architect` | Tier `L0` | Runtime default `Not Run` | Artifact default `Not Produced` | Mutation `downgrade_only`

## When to use & trigger cues
- intent is explicitly a character / person / creature portrait
- before any modeling or scene file is built
- when the consumer is editorial / brand / catalog / cinematic
- Trigger phrases: "portrait of", "character looking at the camera", "headshot", "hero shot of [person / mascot / creature]"

## When not to use (delegation boundaries)
- product hero scenes → use `product-hero-scene-planner` (`references/skill-product-hero-scene-planner.md`; use product-hero-scene-planner)
- environment establishing shots → use `environment-shot` (`references/skill-environment-shot.md`; use environment-shot)
- interior arch viz → use `interior-scene` (`references/skill-interior-scene.md`; use interior-scene)
- multi-character ensemble (this skill is single-subject) → use `intent-to-3d-brief-writer` (`references/skill-intent-to-3d-brief-writer.md`; this skill is single-subject)

## Input & output contract
- Required input `locked_3d_brief` (`object`): Locked 3D brief specifying character subject, expression/pose, and framing intent
- Required input `character_asset_posture` (`object`): Available character model/rig status and material readiness from asset discovery
- Optional input `turntable_or_still_preference` (`string`): Whether the deliverable is a portrait still, bust turntable, or full-body pose
- Output contract: `character_staging_and_pose_plan`, `eyeline_and_portrait_camera_anchors`, `skin_hair_rim_lighting_hooks` (Runtime status: `Not Run`, Artifact status: `Not Produced`, `downgrade_only`).

## Quick-start steps
1. confirm single-subject scope and upstream brief from `intent-to-3d-brief-writer`
2. confirm likeness rights before use if the subject is a real person
3. pin subject identity, pose, expression, wardrobe, framing, lighting, and background
4. record an explicit assumptions register
5. flag needed assets for `asset-discovery`
6. emit handoffs to `camera-composition`, `lighting-material-plan`, and quality checkers with `Runtime status: Not Run` and `Artifact status: Not Produced`

## Safety boundaries & non-goals
- Runtime boundary: Planning-only skill: no modeling, no animation, no render, and no Blender execution. `Runtime status` stays `Not Run` and `Artifact status` stays `Not Produced` (downgrade-only, never upgrade). If the brief is unclear, hand off to `intent-to-3d-brief-writer`.
- Model the character.
- Animate the character.
- Render.
- Run Blender.
